nodes.name: CNOs annealing
nodes.procedure: The nano-diamond powder (an average size of 5 nm) were annealed at 1500 °C with a heating speed of 10 °C min−1, kept for 30 min in vacuum of ~10−2 Pa, and then cooled down to the room temperature naturally.
nodes.source_text: The carbon nano-onions (CNOs) were obtained by annealing nano-diamond powder in a tube furnace... cooled down to the room temperature naturally.

nodes.name: High-pressure M-doped Fe3C@CNOs synthesis
nodes.procedure: Commercial transition-metal powders (Alfa Aesar, ~30 nm) and CNOs (Fe/M/CNOs, 10% M) were mixed in molar ratio of 0.9:0.1:1 (Fe:M:CNOs), and ground for 30 min in the agate mortar (A, ∅80 mm). Then, the mixtures were prepressed into cylindrical block (6.8 mm × 3 mm) within a carbide mould at 20 MPa, and encapsulated into h-BN capsules in glove box (Ar atmosphere, O2 & H2O < 0.1 ppm). The samples were annealed at 800 °C for 15 min under 5.0 GPa with graphite heater, and after heating, the cylindrical blocks were quickly cooled to room temperature by circulating water. Finally, the products were peeled out from the assembly, and ultrasonically washed several times with ethanol.

nodes.characterization_summary: Strong peaks at 35.2°, 37.7°, 39.8° etc. match Fe3C (JCPDS#72-1110); (211) peak at 43.9° shifts to higher angle for FCC@CNOs due to Co substitution causing lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns of FCC@CNOs and Fe3C@CNOs show the strong peaks at 35.2°, 37.7°, 39.8°, 40.6°, 42.9°, 43.8°, 44.6°,45.0°, 45.9°, 48.6°, 49.1°, 51.8°, 54.4°, 56.0° and 58.0°... The diffraction peak at 43.9° is indexed to be (211) crystal plane of Fe3C, which is slightly shifted to higher angles for FCC@CNOs

nodes.characterization_summary: Clear lattice fringes of 0.24 nm corresponding to Fe3C (210) plane; core-shell structure with CNOs shells showing 0.35 nm (002) graphite spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images (Fig. 2d) show the clear lattice fringes of 0.24 nm, corresponding to the (210) crystal plane of Fe3C... The lattice spacing of 0.35 nm for CNOs shells are originated from (002) of graphite.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS-SEM shows atomic ratio Fe:Co = 40.4:4.4 in FCC@CNOs; TEM-EDS mappings show even distribution of Co, Fe, and C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the semi-quantitative analysis using EDS-SEM (Table S2 and Fig. S3f), the atomic ratio of Fe:Co in FCC@CNOs is found to be 40.4:4.4... TEM&HRTEM and EDS elemental mappings (Fig. 2e) further illustrate the even distribution of Co, Fe, and C

nodes.characterization_summary: Type IV isotherm with hysteresis confirms mesoporous character; FCC@CNOs: 112.75 m²/g BET area, 8.99 nm pore size; Fe3C@CNOs: 100.51 m²/g, 8.87 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N2 adsorption/desorption isotherm of FCC@CNOs shows a type IV shape with distinct hysteresis loop... The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of FCC@CNOs is calculated to be 112.75 m² g⁻¹... Fe3C@CNOs also exhibits a hysteresis sorption isotherm curve with average pore size of 8.87 nm with BET surface area of 100.51 m² g⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows ID/IG = 0.941 for FCC@CNOs and 0.942 for Fe3C@CNOs indicating high graphitization degree.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S4b shows that ID/IG values are 0.942 for Fe3C@CNOs and 0.941 for FCC@CNOs, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p3/2: 780.7 & 786.1 eV (Co²⁺), 782.9 eV (Co³⁺); no Fe-C peak at 707.2 eV due to carbide coverage by carbon shells.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution spectrum of Co 2p3/2 (Fig. 2g) can be deconvoluted into three peaks for Co²⁺ 2p3/2 (780.7 and 786.1 eV) and Co³⁺ 2p3/2 (782.9 eV)... the disappearance of BE peak at 707.2 eV, assigned to Fe-C bond in carbide, is attributed to carbides covered by onion-like carbon shells

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl = 99.18 mF/cm² for FCC@CNOs (vs 20.78 mF/cm² for Fe3C@CNOs) measured between 0.1-0.2 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FCC@CNOs presents a capacitance of 99.18 mF cm⁻² nearly 5 times of that of Fe3C@CNOs (20.78 mF cm⁻²) (Fig. 3e), indicating that the specific morphology of FCC@CNOs provides a larger active surface area.

nodes.characterization_summary: At 320 mV overpotential, Rct = 32.6 Ω for FCC@CNOs (vs 376.5 Ω for Fe3C@CNOs, 151.5 Ω FMC@CNOs, 43.9 Ω FNC@CNOs).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The semicircle diameter of the FCC@CNOs (32.6 ohm) is much smaller than those of Fe3C@CNOs (376.5 ohm), FMC@CNOs (151.5 ohm) and FNC@CNOs (43.9 ohm)

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge at 7727.5 eV (between CoO 7725.2 eV and Co2O3 7730.5 eV); Fe K-edge at 7130.5 eV (between FeO 7129.0 eV and FeOOH 7132 eV); Co-C bond 1.9 Å shortens to 1.8 Å after OER.
